markdown:
Today’s AI usage (midnight → ~1:13 PM PT) — checked.

**Grok Bot (spoken only)**
Logged **78%** left now. Soft ceiling if that holds: about **21%/day** to Mon Sep 28 ~8:00 AM PT (~3.8 days). Spoken bar also jumped **43% → 78%** overnight — I will **not** treat that as a refund. You’re right that soft caps were too optimistic last cycle when you hit ~**93% used** before reset; from now on I’ll track **drops only**, ignore rises, and alert on burn rate instead of leftover comfort.

**Hermes today (heavy)**
- **16** sessions (4 CLI + 12 TUI), all primary work on **`grok-4.6` via xAI OAuth** — no DeepSeek coding today.
- **991** API calls · ~**6.7M** input / ~**636k** output tokens (plus large cache-read). Cost marked unknown/$0 in Hermes (subscription path, not OpenRouter cash).
- Active roughly **7:45 AM–1:10 PM PT**. Session chat notes around **10:34–10:35 AM** mention **94% / 93%** — that lines up with **Super Grok** just before/at the ~10:31 AM reset, not the Bot weekly meter. Hermes kept working on xAI after reset (noon and ~1 PM).

**OpenRouter cash**
Balance ≈ **$19.49**. Today ≈ **$0.0004**, week ≈ **$0.0005**, month ≈ **$40.43** — under soft day/week caps; month still under **$50**. Free-model quota **11/1000** used today. Auxiliary Hermes title-gen was DeepSeek flash (~that tiny daily $).

**Chat (`:3001` / `:4006` ai_usage, today only)**
3 calls: **1** real answer (Cohere free, ~6.5k tokens), **2** 404s on free Nemotron (zero tokens). Chat’s logged **$0.0048** does **not** match OpenRouter’s daily field — I’m not combining those until reconciled.

**Going forward on Bot estimates**
1. Spoken % is authority; rises = meter noise.
2. Soft daily max = spoken / days to Monday 8 AM, but warn from **implied burn on drops**.
3. Keep Bot / Super Grok / OpenRouter / Chat as separate ledgers.
4. After the next chunk of Bot work, send another spoken % if you can — that recalibrates faster than my guesses.

Full write-up was `/workspace/ai-usage-today-2026-09-24.md` inside the Bot sandbox (not copied; this JSON is the persistence extract).
